description:
Add production-grade observability to stoa-mail for AWS deployment and regulated-customer readiness.

## Why this issue exists
stoa-mail currently emits structured JSON logs via tracing-subscriber but has no distributed traces, no W3C TraceContext propagation, and no explicit audit event type. For regulated customers (HIPAA, SOC2, PCI-DSS) the following are required: tamper-evident audit logs for all auth/authz events, per-request trace IDs that link every log line to a single request, and a log pipeline that can route security events to a separate log group with tighter retention and access control.

## Scope of this epic
Three deliverables:
1. Add tracing-opentelemetry + OTLP exporter so spans flow to an ADOT collector (→ X-Ray + CloudWatch)
2. Add tower-http TraceLayer to axum router with W3C TraceContext propagation
3. Add a well-known audit = true tracing::Event field on all auth/authz events so the ADOT collector can route them to a separate CloudWatch log group

## Out of scope (infra, not code)
- ADOT collector deployment and configuration
- CloudWatch log group creation, KMS key setup, retention policies
- S3 export with Object Lock for long-term archive
- Prometheus → CloudWatch metric routing (already works via existing /metrics endpoint)

## Acceptance criteria
- cargo build --workspace succeeds with OTEL feature disabled (feature-gated)
- Every HTTP request produces a span with trace_id, method, path, status, duration
- W3C traceparent header from inbound requests is honored (existing trace continues)
- Auth success, auth failure (wrong password, bad token, missing header), and operator-gate rejection each emit a tracing event with audit = true
- Tests verify audit events are emitted (test subscriber captures and asserts fields)
- OTLP exporter is flushed cleanly on shutdown (no lost spans on SIGTERM)
title: OpenTelemetry observability: OTLP traces, TraceLayer, audit events
